Variants.Content: The Dahar family was named in the history of the Narrow Sea by Krahas Dahal. Krahas once represented the Third Daughter Kingdom in fighting pirates on the Stepstone Islands. Later, he gained the reputation of the "Crab Feeder" for his cruel treatment of prisoners and heavy taxes, and was defeated in the Island War. That past incident shows that the wealth of the Myr family is closely connected with the Strait shipping, and also shows that protecting trade routes and plundering trade routes are sometimes separated only by taxes and force. Myr is renowned for its fine craftsmanship and trade, with lenses, lace, carpets, dyes and Myr-style crossbows all requiring skilled craftsmen and imported raw materials. Cities were dominated by wealthy merchants, governors, and industrial interests, with wealth supported by slave labor and the skills of free artisans.
Entry Dahar Exquisite goods are highly profitable, but a shortage of raw materials or a wrong move in diplomacy can shut down an entire workshop.
Entry Dahar Nobles can sell lace thousands of miles away, but the person who really makes the needlework flawless is the person who hurts his eyes by the window.

The family crest is just a facade, the real weight of the family is whether they can protect their fiefdom, honor their engagements, and rally people in times of crisis.
